The complainant has not produced transaction statement for the relevant period i.e after 13-08-2010 when the V.V. Securities came into existence and thus there is absolutely no evidence on behalf of the complainant to fasten the criminal liability upon the accused prior to 13-08-2010.
The onus was heavily upon the complainant to prove the criminal liability of accused in order to sustain the commission of offences charged with.

It is pertinent to mention here that as per the procedure/practice prevailing regarding sale and purchase of shares in the Demat account, all the transactions take place through the Banking channel and in the Rampat Singh Vs. Ved Prakash Aggarwal & Ors.
Demat account electronically.

sentences.text: There is no procedure for selling the shares physically once they have been transferred to the Demat account and the sale and purchase of the shares are done electronically and proceeds of the shares stand credited into the Demat account of the owner.

The entire process of share trading in the Demat account takes place automatically (electronically)
without the intervention of any third party and the proceeds of sale can be transferred from demat account into the bank account linked with the same demat account.

Therefore, neither the depository nor the Broker or any other third person can conduct sale/ purchase transaction of shares which have been Dematerialized in the account of the share holder without his permission.

12. No doubt accused namely Virender Saini and Varun Aggarwal have been shown as authorized persons of V.V. Securities in CW1/2 but V.V. Securities came into existence on 13-08-2010 and no transactions details involving the accused or the details of transaction carried out by the accused persons without the authority of the complainant have been produced by the complainant.
There is nothing on the file in order to show that any transaction took place through the brokerage firm of V.V Securities.

Therefore, in the absence of any evidence to the effect that the accused were involved in the sale of shares of the complainant and the sale proceeds were misappropriated no offence can be said to have been committed.
So much so, there is absolutely nothing on the file in order to show as to what happened with the shares which were in Demat account of the complainant and his daughter in law Ms. Sonia.
The complainant ought to have obtained the transaction details of Demat account with Consortium Securities Pvt. Ltd. after June 2010
in order to ascertain to whom the said shares were transferred and at what rate and where the sale proceeds were credited.
There is nothing on the file to prove the allegations that the sale proceeds of shares were siphoned off.

However, the law down in the above referred authorities is not in dispute, but the-onus is heavy upon the complainant to approve unauthorised transactions in the Demant account of the complainant and siphoning off the funds of the sale proceeds from the said Demat account of the complainant by leading cogent and positive evidence beyond shadow of reasonable doubt and in the absence of such evidence the accused becomes entitled for acquittal.
